subtopic: GPU memory hierarchy / bandwidth / access rules
learningObjective: Distinguish structural and access-pattern properties of NVIDIA GPU memory tiers (register file, shared memory, constant memory, global memory).
stem: Which of the following statements about the A100 (sm_80) memory hierarchy are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Aggregate global-memory (HBM2e) bandwidth on the A100 board is higher than the aggregate on-chip shared-memory bandwidth summed across all SMs, since HBM stacks scale linearly with pin count and channels.

Shared memory is bank-organized: warp threads accessing distinct addresses in the same bank serialize (bank conflict); global memory has no banks but obeys coalescing rules on 32/64/128 B transactions.
Constant memory accesses in which all threads of a warp read the same address are broadcast, avoiding a per-thread memory transaction and delivering the value in one cycle to the whole warp.
The per-SM register file (65,536 × 32-bit ≈ 256 KB) is larger than the per-SM configurable L1/shared-memory partition (up to 192 KB total on A100).

explanation: A: The A100 register file is 65,536 × 4 B = 256 KB per SM, whereas L1/SMEM is at most 192 KB per SM (configurable). C: Shared memory is bank-organized and conflicts serialize; global memory uses coalescing (bytes-per-transaction rules), not banks. D: Constant memory is optimized for broadcast when all threads in a warp read the same address. B is false: aggregate shared-memory bandwidth across all SMs is much higher than aggregate HBM bandwidth (SRAM ≫ HBM per-byte throughput).

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect: HBM bandwidth (~ 2 TB/s aggregate) is lower than the sum of per-SM shared-memory bandwidth over all 108 SMs (each SMEM partition supplies many TB/s effective).
optionExplanations.B: Correct: bank conflicts affect shared memory; coalescing affects global memory.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: constant-memory broadcast is a documented CUDA optimization.

assumptions: Shared-memory bank width = 32-bit (4 bytes) per bank.
nonImplications: Does not imply that programmers should always favor shared memory; small kernels may perform better with only register/L1 usage.
Does not imply that constant-memory broadcast is used automatically for uniform accesses to global memory.

distractorRationales.A: Reverses the ranking of on-chip vs. off-chip aggregate bandwidth.
